_about: Upgrade paths (owner 2026-11-14, rebuilt for the upgrade paths plan 2026-11-15: docs/revisions/UPGRADE_PATHS_PLAN.md). Every track belongs to one of five sections (Energy, Biology, Health, Science, Communication); a section's tracks are chosen at its core spot (sections[].core_station_ids). The colony finishes ONE build a day, voted in the evening Plan block (scripts/upgrades/colony_builds.gd). A track has `levels` levels (V1..Vn, V1 = today's model); its level lives in state.levels[track] (missing = 1). costs[i] is what reaching level i+1 costs: spare parts (state.parts) and ores (state.ores.stock[ore_id]); costs[0] is always {}. upkeep_kw[i] is the extra power the track draws at level i+1 (total, not per step). Effects are lists indexed by level - 1, read with AreaLevels.effect(state, track, key, default). A fork (forks{}) is a permanent choice at one level of a track; the chosen side's effects override the track's (state.build.forks[fork_id]). requires{level: {track: level}} = another track must be at least that level first. Numbers follow the plan's big-jump-first curve (+60 %, +30 %, +15 %, +8 %) and are designer balance, never NASA figures, unless source_ids say so. The rover is bought like every track since 2026-11-15; its garage modules still upgrade on their own.

choices.name: Regenerative fuel cells
choices.text: Sun power by day splits water into gas; at night the fuel cells turn it back into power.

stages.3: Fuel cell tank farm: sun power by day becomes night power
stages.4: Bigger tank farm and a second fuel cell stack

choices.name: Small fission reactor (10 kW)
choices.text: A small nuclear reactor parked away from the base behind a dirt wall. Steady power day and night, dust or not.

stages.3: 10 kW fission reactor behind a dirt wall
stages.4: Bigger reactor: 13 kW day and night

tracks.name: Day power
stages: Dusty solar panels
Crew cleans the panels every sol
Dust shield: the panels clean themselves
Sun trackers turn the panels to the sun
Multi-junction cells: dark, high-power panels

effect_notes.solar_factor: balance: multiplies every tracker's daytime output on top of the dust and storm rules. Was energy.solar_factor before 2026-11-15 (energy is now night power, its solar_factor stays 1.0).

tracks.name: Night power
stages: Today's battery rows
Second battery bank and a bigger inverter
Fork: fuel cells or a fission reactor
Bigger fuel cells or a bigger reactor

effect_notes.battery_capacity_factor: balance: applied once to capacities.battery_kwh at the level change (AreaLevelActions / ColonyBuilds). 700 -> 1,120 kWh.
effect_notes.night_kw: from the night_power fork choice (fuel_cell 6/8 kW at night only, reactor 10/13 kW day and night).
effect_notes.solar_factor: kept for old code: solar now grows with day_power.solar_factor.

tracks.name: Storm power
stages: No wind power
Test wind turbine (about 0.5 kW)
One big wind turbine on the ridge
Wind farm: more turbines on the ridge

effect_notes.wind_kw: balance: turbine power in clear, calm daytime air; the power model may raise it at night and in dust storms (wind is strongest then, Hartwick et al. 2023).

tracks.name: Use less power
stages: Old lights and heaters
LED lights: 10 % less power
Insulation: 10 % less again
Heat recovery: 15 % less again
The oxygen plant runs by day, when the sun shines

tracks.name: Food, water and recycling
stages: One layer of grow beds: fresh salad
Two-layer rack, urine processor and a compost bin
Three-layer staple farm and a brine processor (98 % water back)
Four-layer vertical farm, water from clay and ice
Closed loop: aeroponics, insects eat the scraps

effect_notes.water_recovery: share of used water the colony gets back (ISS reached 98 % with its brine processor, plan source 55).

tracks.name: Garden dome
stages: Bare planters
Ground cover and herbs
Shrubs and a raised bed ring
Dwarf fruit trees and a full canopy

effect_notes.plant_o2_kg_per_hour: NASA-derived (S20 BVAD Rev2 Table 4-91: lettuce gives 7.78 g O2 per m2 per day, a sol average). Planted area is balance: V2 31 m2, V3 62 m2, V4 108 m2 of leafy plants, so 31 x 7.78 / 24 = 0.010, 62 x 7.78 / 24 = 0.020, 108 x 7.78 / 24 = 0.035 kg O2 per game hour. One crew member breathes 0.0373 kg/h (S20 Table 3-31), so the full garden covers about one crew member in four. Plants also take up 1.375 kg CO2 per kg O2 (physics, agrees with Table 4-91).

tracks.name: Life support (air)
stages: Today's air plant: tanks, CO₂ scrubber, electrolysis
Second scrubber bed and an O₂ buffer tank
Twin electrolysers and a Sabatier reactor: oxygen back from CO₂
Backup plant that makes oxygen from Mars air
Nearly closed loop: most oxygen comes back

effect_notes.o2_recovery: share of breathed oxygen won back from CO2 (Sabatier ~50 %, plan §4.3).

tracks.name: Medical care
stages: First aid and dosimeter badges
Vitals monitors, ultrasound and an IV stand
Second bed with a body scanner arch, small lab
Surgical light, imaging and a long-life pharmacy

effect_notes.isolation_hours_factor: multiplies how long a crewmate at the radiation limit stays in the isolation bed (plan §5.2).

tracks.name: Protection: shields, suits and airlocks
stages: Bare hab: 4 h suit oxygen, basic airlock
Storm shelter lined with water tanks; 6 h suits
Dirt bags on the roofs; dust-proof seals, faster airlock
3D-printed dirt shell; 8 h suits and a storm vest
Water and ice walls, buried; suitports

effect_notes.radiation_indoor_factor: share of the ~0.67 mSv/sol surface dose (Curiosity RAD, plan source 43) that still reaches the crew indoors. A thin dirt layer helps very little (plan source 47).
effect_notes.storm_shelter_factor: share of a solar storm's dose that reaches crew in the shelter.

tracks.name: Lab and materials
stages: Workbench: tell ores apart
Laser spectrometer: see what is in a rock
X-ray mineral analyser: find the exact minerals
Materials lab: turns ore into spare parts, glass and bricks
Research station: faster science, opens the last level of other paths

effect_notes.parts_per_sol_from_ore: spare parts the materials lab can make each sol from ore in stock (the ores system spends the ore).

tracks.name: Scout drone
stages: Manual drone: you fly it yourself
Semi-autonomous: pre-scouts an area and reports its minerals
Smart search: "find iron" goes to known spots
Full scan: ground radar scans anywhere

effect_notes.flight_seconds: game scale for a ~560 x 530 m map (plan §6.2); Ingenuity flew 90-169 s.

tracks.name: Crew rover
stages: Open rover: suit oxygen is the limit
Bigger battery packs: reach the middle ring
Sealed cabin with a suitport: also a storm shelter
Fuel-cell range extender: reach the far ring
Nuclear power cart and a sample arm with a laser

effect_notes._: The rover's driving numbers per level live in scripts/core/rover_balance.gd (cabin_level 3, fuel_cell_level 4, rtg_level 5, sample_arm_level 5); these flags only say the same in words. Bought like every other track since 2026-11-15 (was: followed the garage modules). The garage modules still upgrade as before; the look (scripts/upgrades/stages/rover_stages.gd) shows both.

tracks.name: Ore survey
stages: Ores near the base
Middle ring ores show on the map
Far ring ores show on the map
Every ore, with the mission that found it

tracks.name: Comms
stages: Fixed radio: talk to people near you; the suit radio does not send
Map wall and suit radio near the Command Room (30 s delay outside)
Relay rack: suit radio across the base (10 s delay outside)
Screen wall and roof mast: 2 s delay, clear words
Big roof dish: instant, clear radio across the whole map

effect_notes.suit_radio_delay_s: -1 = the suit radio does not send outside (after the tutorial's T01 fix only). The real suit-to-suit delay on Mars is near zero; the game's delay stands for a weak signal through a busy relay (plan §7.1).
effect_notes.storm_warning_factor: multiplies the warning time before dust storms and solar storms.
